Python cells with `renderings: [light, dark]`, which draw one plot for each
color mode, as [Renderings (R)](s-renderings-r.html) does for R cells. The page
shows the one for its mode (the toggle in the navbar), and so does the viewer.
Each one is worth opening in light and dark mode.

Each case shows its source above the plot: Jupyter leaves `panzoom:` out of the
echoed code of a cell.

The plots are drawn with this helper:

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np


def wave(k=1, ink="black", paper="white", col="#3B7DB8"):
    """Draw a shaded sine wave.

    k: wave number; the curve completes k cycles.
    ink: color for the axes, labels, and title.
    paper: plot background color, or "none" to leave it transparent.
    col: color for the curve and its shaded area.
    """
    x = np.linspace(0, 4 * np.pi, 400)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 5))
    fig.patch.set_facecolor(paper)
    ax.set_facecolor(paper)
    ax.fill_between(x, np.sin(k * x), color=col, alpha=0.35, linewidth=0)
    ax.plot(x, np.sin(k * x), color=col, linewidth=2)
    ax.set(title=f"Wave {k}", xlabel="x", ylabel="sin(kx)")
    ax.title.set_color(ink)
    ax.xaxis.label.set_color(ink)
    ax.yaxis.label.set_color(ink)
    ax.tick_params(colors=ink)
    for spine in ax.spines.values():
        spine.set_color(ink)
    plt.show()
```

## Light and dark renderings {expect-open="panzoom"}

A cell with two plots: black ink on white for light mode, and light gray ink on
near-black for dark mode. It opens in panzoom with the plot for the current
color mode.

````source
```{{python}}
#| panzoom: true
#| renderings: [light, dark]
#| fig-alt: "A sine curve in blue on a background matching the page"
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Wave 3: y = sin(3x); the area between the curve and y = 0 is shaded.

wave(3)
wave(3, ink="#D9D9D9", paper="#1E1E1E", col="#7FB8E6")
```
````

```{python}
#| panzoom: true
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
#| fig-alt: "A sine curve in blue on a background matching the page"
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Wave 3: y = sin(3x); the area between the curve and y = 0 is shaded.

wave(3)
wave(3, ink="#D9D9D9", paper="#1E1E1E", col="#7FB8E6")
```

## Transparent renderings {expect-open="panzoom"}

A cell with two plots on a transparent background: black ink for light mode and
light gray ink for dark mode. It opens in panzoom with the plot for the current
color mode.

````source
```{{python}}
#| panzoom: true
#| renderings: [light, dark]
#| fig-alt: "A sine curve in blue with axes in the text color"
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Wave 4: y = sin(4x); the area between the curve and y = 0 is shaded.

wave(4, paper="none")
wave(4, ink="#D9D9D9", paper="none")
```
````

```{python}
#| panzoom: true
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
#| fig-alt: "A sine curve in blue with axes in the text color"
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Wave 4: y = sin(4x); the area between the curve and y = 0 is shaded.

wave(4, paper="none")
wave(4, ink="#D9D9D9", paper="none")
```

## Gallery with light and dark renderings {expect-open="panzoom" expect-steps="true"}

Two cells with `renderings: [light, dark]`, joined by `group: renderings`. The
gallery steps through the two plots for the current mode.

````source
```{{python}}
#| panzoom:
#|   group: renderings
#| renderings: [light, dark]
#| fig-alt: "A sine curve in blue with axes in the text color"
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Wave 5: y = sin(5x); the area between the curve and y = 0 is shaded.

wave(5, paper="none")
wave(5, ink="#D9D9D9", paper="none")
````

## Renderings in the other order {expect-open="panzoom"}

A cell with `renderings: [dark, light]`: the first plot, with light gray ink, is
for dark mode, and the second, with black ink, for light mode. It opens in
panzoom with the plot for the current color mode, as with the default order.

````source
```{{python}}
#| panzoom: true
#| renderings: [dark, light]
#| fig-alt: "A sine curve in blue with axes in the text color"
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Wave 2: y = sin(2x); the area between the curve and y = 0 is shaded.

wave(2, ink="#D9D9D9", paper="none")
wave(2, paper="none")
```
````

```{python}
#| panzoom: true
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [dark, light]
#| fig-alt: "A sine curve in blue with axes in the text color"
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Wave 2: y = sin(2x); the area between the curve and y = 0 is shaded.

wave(2, ink="#D9D9D9", paper="none")
wave(2, paper="none")
```
